trigger: An operator command fails before the intended runtime gate, including 404 source lookup, malformed PowerShell tokens, missing downloaded files, terminal closure, or lost visible diagnostics.

steps.action: Classify the earliest observed failure boundary: source-resolution, transport-corruption, shell-control, prerequisite, downstream-runtime, or evidence-resolution.
steps.gate: One boundary is named without promoting downstream proof.

steps.action: Preserve the failed command and exact stderr/stdout as local operational evidence; do not commit operator-machine data.
steps.gate: Failure evidence is available for comparison.

steps.action: Re-resolve the requested repository ref and every required file independently of the failed command.
steps.gate: The source exists or the exact missing ref/file is identified.

steps.action: Run the focused command-delivery validator against the repaired command form and regression fixtures.
steps.gate: Corruption and shell-control fixtures behave deterministically.

steps.action: Repair harness maps, workflows, registries, skill, report, hook, or validators when the failure class was not already enforced.
steps.gate: A fresh agent can discover the trap before reproducing it.

steps.action: Commit and push the harness repair on an isolated branch; open or update the owning PR.
Only after harness validation, provide the smallest executable operator command that advances to the previously unproven runtime gate.
steps.gate: The command preserves the parent terminal and prints the canonical downstream artifact.

stopConditions: Source ref or required file cannot be resolved.
Repair would require product-code mutation outside the declared lane.
The next proof requires credentials, protected runtime access, destructive reset, or another unauthorized capability.
proofCeiling: Failure classification and harness repair only. Runtime success must be earned again from the downstream owning artifact.
